note: Great Moravia and the East Frankish kingdom maintained a complex relationship of conflict and dependence from Moravia's foundation (c. 830) through its destruction (906). Rastislav of Moravia sought independence from Frankish ecclesiastical domination by requesting Byzantine missionaries (862) — resulting in Cyril and Methodius's Slavic mission. His successor Sviatopluk negotiated a treaty with Louis the German (874) while maintaining autonomy. East Frankish princes allied with Magyar invaders who destroyed Moravia (906); the Franks subsequently failed to prevent Magyar raids westward.

_quarry.structural_significance: The East Frankish-Moravian conflict drives Moravia toward Byzantine Christianity; the resulting Slavic alphabet and liturgy transform the cultural trajectory of all Slavic peoples; the Frankish failure to absorb Moravia, followed by Magyar destruction, creates the political vacuum in the Danube basin
